name: application-log-viewer
title: Log Viewer
description: Monospace log stream with severity coloring, toggleable level filter chips (info/warn/error/debug), and an auto-scroll toggle — a debugging staple for admin panels, deploy logs, and observability dashboards.
useWhen: Streaming or displaying structured log entries with a severity level per line.
Users need to filter noisy output down to specific levels (e.g. only WARN and ERROR).
A live-updating stream should stay pinned to the newest entry unless the user opts out via auto-scroll.
avoidWhen: The content isn't line-oriented or timestamped — use a plain code block or terminal-blocks instead.
You need syntax-highlighted source code, not runtime log output — use code-editor-block instead.
The dataset is small and static — a plain list or table is simpler than a scrolling log panel.
responsiveBehavior: The panel is a fixed-width block with an internal max-height scroll region; filter chips wrap onto multiple lines on narrow viewports.
accessibility: The scrolling log region carries role='log' and aria-live='polite' so new entries are announced without interrupting.
Level filter chips and the auto-scroll toggle are real buttons with aria-pressed reflecting their on/off state.
Severity is conveyed by both the level text label (INFO/WARN/ERROR/DEBUG) and color, not color alone.

variants.title: Log viewer
variants.description: Dark terminal-style log panel with INFO/WARN/ERROR entries, active level filter chips, and auto-scroll enabled, on a light page.
accessibility: The log panel keeps its dark terminal chrome regardless of page theme, matching common log-viewer conventions.

variants.title: Log viewer (Dark)
variants.description: Log panel with the same entries and controls, deepened to sit inside a fully dark app shell.
accessibility: Level text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast against the near-black panel background.
